title: Six Worcestershire pubs said to be haunted by ghosts, footsteps and flying plates
excerpt: The so-called spooky season has arrived and Worcestershire is lucky to have plenty of atmospheric pubs to celebrate in.
content:
THE spooky season has arrived and Worcestershire is lucky to have plenty of atmospheric pubs to celebrate in.

Some of Worcestershire's popular boozers are also well-known for their history and ghost stories.

With Halloween fast approaching, Visit Worcestershire has shared the six "most haunted" pubs in the county:

The Mug House, Claines, Worcester

The Mug House, Claines (Image: James Connell/Newsquest)

The Mug House, located beside the ancient churchyard in Claines, is said to be haunted by a ghost named Bert.

There have been reports of unexplained footsteps and pint glasses swinging like pendulums.

Ye Olde Black Cross, Bromsgrove

Dating back to around 1640, Ye Olde Black Cross in Bromsgrove is said to be haunted by the spirits of condemned criminals, a little girl, and a cavalier soldier.

Unexplained images have reportedly appeared on CCTV, and the inn is said to have two haunted rooms.

The Cardinal's Hat, Worcester

The Cardinal's Hat, Worcester (Image: Newsquest)

The Cardinal's Hat is one of Worcester's oldest pubs and is known for its spooky occurrences.

There have been sightings of a little blonde girl running across the first floor, and some people have reported sudden changes in room temperature.

The Little Pack Horse, Bewdley

Dating back to the 15th century, The Little Pack Horse is known for its spooky tales.

Former staff have reportedly heard children's footsteps and faint giggling echoing across the upper floor.

The Fleece Inn, Bretforton

The Fleece Inn, Bretforton (Image: James Connell/Newsquest)

The Fleece Inn in Bretforton is said to be haunted by its former landlady, Lola Taplin.

There have been reports of plates and sandwich boxes being mysteriously thrown to the floor.

The Black Boy Inn, Bewdley

Dating back to 1466, the Black Boy Inn on Wyre Hill is one of Bewdley's historic landmarks.

With centuries of history behind it, this old inn offers plenty of atmosphere for those exploring Worcestershire's past and its ghostly tales.
